articles.title: Seabirds racing home over the ocean can get jet-lagged
articles.description: A long flight home from feeding grounds messes with birds' internal clocks.
articles.content: Flying across several time zones often causes jet lag, a feeling when the body insists it's the middle of the night while the clock says it's lunchtime. Now it turns out this nuisance is not exclusive to humans. A new Science study on Manx shearwaters, seabirds that can fly hundreds of kilometers a day over the North Atlantic, shows they jet-lag themselves during their excursions.
